rv.q: You will be rewarded with a filthily funny 90 minutes or so of broadbrush satire which will have you giggling like a naughty schoolchild all the way home.
The ribald laughter The Windsors provokes can’t be denied.
Despite the sharpness of its satire, it feels timid and unambitious as a piece of theatre.
It’s fitfully amusing, startlingly crude at times and not a little cruel.
In its own way, this feels comparable to that royal disaster.
The Windsors: Endgame is a right royal pantomime and jolly good fun.
The Windsors gets a lot of things right when it could have done a whole lot more wrong: with a royal parody that's exactly what you'd probably want to be signing up for.

The show is well-done fun and while the royals themselves will be keen to give this a wide berth, many of their subjects, not to mention returning West End tourists, could do a good deal worse than witness the Prince of Wales parodied on the stage of the Prince of Wales.
Of course it’s ridiculous, but that’s what it sets out to be and its done with panache and an energy that sometimes swamps itself.
Given our national relish for both monarchy and rude jokes, my instinct is that this one will reign and reign.
This regal family manages to have a pop at everyone from Prince Andrew to Jamie Oliver, and try as you might feign indignation, it is viciously funny.

cn.t: Critics find this crude royal satire fitfully funny but uneven—fans of the TV series may be disappointed by its transition to stage, though those embracing its filthy, pantomime-style irreverence will enjoy a solidly entertaining night.
